evidence: Cic. Fam. 1.3.1: magna negōtia et ampla et expedīta habet
terms.comment: Business of every kind, a day’s work or trade: the opposite of ōtium. In the plural, business interests. To run a business, negōtium exercēre (Traupman 131).

evidence: Cic. Off. 1.151: mercātūra autem, sī tenuis est, sordida putanda est (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: To be in trade: mercātūrās facere (Cic. Verr. 2.5.72).

phrases.latin: cum sē Syrācūsās ōtiandī, nōn negōtiandī causā contulisset
phrases.english: when he had gone to Syracuse on holiday, not on business

phrases.latin: beātus ille quī procul negōtiīs, ut prīsca gēns mortālium
phrases.english: happy the man who, far from business, like the first race of men …

sources: Lewis & Short: negotium · Lewis & Short: negotior · Lewis & Short: mercatura · Lewis & Short: negotiator
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. business: do business.
